content.title: Samson PC optimization guide: Best settings for visuals and performance
content.text: Samson is a newly released, massive open-world game built using the Unreal Engine 5. The game incorporates Lumen and Nanite and is extremely CPU-bound to begin with. Currently, the game, with default settings or quality presets, will cause performance issues on your system, regardless of whether your system meets the developers' official recommendations. The settings below are fine-tuned for any modern system with RT support and at least 8GB of VRAM. We recommend dialing these in at any given resolution and customizing them accordingly based on your performance expectations. Frame generation is recommended to alleviate the CPU-bound nature. For GPUs that do not support in-game frame generation, we recommend using third-party solutions such as Lossless Scaling. Note: Some aspects of this article are subjective and reflect the writer’s opinion. This guide is also inspired by the original optimization guide from Benchmark King's YouTube Channel. Read more: Dell G15 vs Acer Nitro V 15: Which gaming laptop should you choose for the best performance? Best settings to play Samson on PC Best setting for Samson (Image via Liquid Swords) The biggest issue in Samson is how the lighting is implemented. If your GPU supports RT (DXR), the game will automatically force hardware Lumen, which tanks CPU performance. The fix, limited to Nvidia cards only, is to use Nvidia Profile Inspector and disable RT support within the game, which will trick the game into using software Lumen, which is much more lenient on the CPU. That being said, use upscaling only if shimmering and aliasing issues bother you; otherwise, try to keep the game as GPU-bound as possible. This is because upscaling reduces the internal resolution, making the game CPU-bound. Also, on the Nvidia side, Ray Reconstruction also doesn't do much, and, as of now, enabling it introduces more noise in the rendered image. To get better performance without ruining visuals, these are the settings that matter: Global Illumination: Balanced/QualityShadows: PerformanceTextures: Balanced (Can increase to higher values on GPUs above 8GB VRAM)Effects: PerformanceReflections: Balanced (Higher values introduce shimmering and aliasing issues)View Distance: High/UltraHair Strands: Off (Reduces CPU load)CategorySettingRecommended ValueDisplayWindow ModeWindowed Fullscreen / FullscreenResolutionNative Monitor ResolutionUpscalingTypeDLSS / TSRQualityQuality/Native AA (Preferred)Frame GenerationOn (FSR or Third-party if applicable)QualityAuto-SetCustomPresetCustomGlobal IlluminationBalanced / QualityShadowsPerformanceAnti-AliasingUltra (if using TSR)View DistanceHigh / UltraTexturesBalanced (Increase if VRAM > 8GB)EffectsPerformanceReflectionsBalancedPost ProcessingPersonal PreferencePost ProcessingMotion BlurPersonal PreferenceDepth of FieldPersonal PreferenceFilm GrainPersonal PreferenceAdvancedVertical SyncUser PreferenceHair StrandsOffFrame Rate LimitGeneralUnlimited (or match monitor refresh rate)Background30 FPS (Preference)Menu144 FPS (Preference)On Battery60 FPS (Preference) Read more: Alienware 16X Aurora review: Not a maxed-out monster, but the sweet spot most gamers actually need Was this article helpful?
